<reason>A made the stronger comparative case: prioritize the larger reachable deficit rather than make digital expansion wait because physical provision remains incomplete. A answered both pressure questions directly and consistently compared existing assets and additional costs. B established plausible reasons to expand physical and creative opportunities, but did not establish its claimed national comparison of unmet enrichment needs. Calling those background assertions documented data, equating devices with enrichment, and dismissing transportation barriers left A’s central challenge unanswered.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A decisively challenged B’s override condition requiring fully funded, staffed physical/arts programs before digital could take priority. This exposed the difference between a needs-sensitive presumption and B’s restrictive sequencing rule. B’s closing claimed those rules were identical without resolving that contradiction.</best_rebuttal>
